text:
maya: Quick heads-up — ran a SmoothQuant + activation-aware (AWQ) mix on redwood-llm-14b-long with 64k context. Sharing quick notes and links.

oliver: Nice. Which exact quant stack/config did you run?

maya: Short config snippet I used:
```yaml
model: redwood-llm-14b-long
context: 65536
quant:
  ffn: awq-int8
  attn: smoothquant-int8
act_scale: per_layer
fp8_fallback: true
chunk_size: 4096
batch: 1
kv_cache: sharded
```

toni: Results? numbers please. :chart_with_upwards_trend:

maya: Eval suite (mix of long-context QA, summarization, and multi-hop):
- MRR@5 delta vs fp16: AWQ+SQ = -0.7%, GPTQ-int8 = -2.8%, FP8 mix = -0.3%
- Perplexity delta: AWQ+SQ = +0.8 ppl, GPTQ = +3.2 ppl
- F1 (multi-hop QA): AWQ+SQ = -1.2%, GPTQ = -4.5%

raj: Those are impressively small for AWQ+SQ. Was KV cache enabled for the 64k runs? and what about batching?

maya: KV cache ON (sharded across 4 GPUs), batch_size=1 for tail-latency tests. Also tried batch=4 for throughput bench.

maya: Observed memory behaviors: peak VRAM (per GPU) fp16=61GB, AWQ+SQ=56GB (-8%), FP8 mix=52GB.

eva: Did you check instruction-following/logprob regressions? any sharp drop in calibration?

maya: Token-logprob traces show modest flattening in some FFN-dominated layers. Calibration shift small; we logged per-token logprob diffs for ~1k samples. Link in S3.

bench-bot: Uploaded metrics: s3://redwood-expts/sq-awq-14b-64k-1783456789/metrics.json

toni: Did you try per-layer act-aware rescale vs global smoothquant scaling?

maya: Yes — per-layer act-rescale + smoothquant wins for quality. Numbers: MRR delta -0.3% (best) vs -0.7% for global scaling; cost ~+2% VRAM.

oliver: Latency numbers? token-level and end-to-end for 1k tokens?

maya: Median token-latency (1k gen): fp16=21ms, AWQ+SQ=18ms, GPTQ=16ms (GPTQ fastest but degrades quality more). End-to-end 1k tokens: fp16=21s, AWQ+SQ=18s.

raj: Any KV-cache get/set spikes under concurrency? that's often a killer for long context.

maya: KV get median 3.2ms, 95th=11ms under 16 concurrent streams when sharded. When we pinned KV cache to single-device (no sharding) 95th dropped to 6.5ms but GPU memory pressure increased.

eva: How did FP8 behave? activation overflows?

maya: FP8 needed per-layer activation clipping + act-aware rescale. With that FP8 runs were stable but quality slightly worse than AWQ+SQ in our tasks. FP8 wins on peak memory but loses a bit on multi-hop QA.

maya: Also tried hybrid quant: FP8 on FFN, AWQ-int8 on attention. That gave good tradeoff: MRR delta ~ -0.4%, peak VRAM -10%.

toni: Any notable regression cases (text corruption, hallucination spikes)?

maya: Two failure modes: (1) long prefix repetition when activation scale underestimated — mitigated with act-clipping; (2) subtle answer-swap in multi-hop where chain-of-thought tokens had lower logprob. We flagged those prompts.

maya: Quick command used to run eval harness:
`python tools/eval_longctx.py --model redwood-llm-14b-long --quant awq+smooth --context 65536 --kv sharded --out s3://...`

oliver: Good. Can you add a route and fallback to fp16 for production requests where MRR delta > 1%?

maya: Yes — creating a canary with fallback policy. Also adding regression alarms if MRR delta > 1% and F1 drop > 1.5%.

toni: Actionable items?

maya: 1) Re-run AWQ+SmoothQuant with per-layer act-rescale and 3 random seeds on the eval set (maya).
2) Run hybrid FP8-FFN + AWQ-attn variant (oliver).
3) Add perf + quality dashboards to Console (toni).
4) Add automated regression alarm and baseline snapshots (eva).

deploy-bot: Canary deploy scheduled for dedicated pool `sq-14b-64k-canary` on 2026-03-25T09:00:00Z (will run 24h smoke tests).

maya: Awesome — thanks. Will post updated metrics when the three seeds finish. :thumbsup:
